reason: FAQ Compliance answer: implemented the controls necessary to enable you to meet HIPAA requirements and is an in-scope service in the PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance; both displays verbatim.
FAQ states LDAPS in both client and server roles and, as a server, ports 636 (SSL) and 389 (TLS); the certificate condition is in the following paragraph for Standard and Enterprise.

What-is page: MFA gives an additional layer of security when users access AWS applications from the Internet; because AD is an LDAP directory it serves Linux SSH authentication and other LDAP-enabled applications.

MFA page: must have an MFA solution that is a RADIUS server or an MFA plugin to a RADIUS server; the built-in RADIUS client connects, the RADIUS server validates username and OTP, then AD authenticates the user.

Pricing page: for each managed directory AWS creates the minimum two domain controllers automatically for high availability and you can add more; admin guide: the pair is in your VPC across different Availability Zones.
FAQ: does not allow direct host access to domain controllers via Remote Desktop Connection, PowerShell Remoting, Telnet, or SSH; claim matches exactly.
Admin account page Note: AWS has exclusive control of the Domain Administrator and Enterprise Administrator privileged users and groups so AWS can perform operational management.
FAQ: add domain controllers using the Directory Service console or API; promoting EC2 instances to domain controllers manually is not supported.
FAQ: for Standard and Enterprise Editions AWS does not provide any migration tools; you establish a strategy including password resets. Edition scope kept.
What-gets-created page Note states exactly that AWS does not allow installation of monitoring agents on the domain controllers.
What-is page: by adding Microsoft Entra Connect, and optionally AD FS, you can sign in to Office 365 and other cloud applications with credentials stored in AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
FAQ: synchronize identities to Azure AD with Azure AD Connect and use AD FS with AWS Managed Microsoft AD to authenticate Office 365 users; the claim only omits the AD FS version (Windows 2016).
FAQ: Standard and Enterprise Editions can be a resource forest of primarily computers and groups with trust relationships to your directory on premises or in the cloud.

Admin guide: Standard and Enterprise create new managed domains that establish resource forests with trusts to existing domains on premises, in AWS or multi-cloud; identities stay in existing domains.
FAQ: AWS provides compute, storage and memory; you declare requirements by selecting the edition (Standard, Enterprise, Hybrid); for more resources add domain controllers.
FAQ: Standard and Enterprise editions support schema extensions submitted as an LDIF file; you may extend but not modify the core schema.
Join page: seamlessly join an EC2 instance when launched, or launch and join from the Directory Service console with Systems Manager Automation; both quoted.

Quote allows AD ports only from the VPC's primary IPv4 CIDR block or its IPv6 CIDR block; the claim says 'the VPC's CIDR block' and drops 'primary', so secondary VPC CIDRs would wrongly read as allowed by default. Rest (no Elastic IPs, local VPC only, rules changeable) is supported.
Quotas table row 180 days plus footnote: maximum supported age of a manual snapshot is 180 days, cannot be changed, due to Tombstone-Lifetime; cannot restore from an older snapshot.
FAQ: Standard Edition includes 1 GB of directory object storage, can support up to 5,000 users or 30,000 objects; the estimate condition is stated in the same answer.
Admin guide: configure trusts with your self-managed AD, providing users and groups with access to resources in either domain using IAM Identity Center.
What-is page: applications use credentials stored in AWS Managed Microsoft AD, or connect with a trust and use credentials from an AD on premises or on EC2 Windows.
FAQ: directories are deployed across two Availability Zones in a region by default and connected to your VPC; matches claim and default qualifier.
What-is page When to use: best choice for actual AD features (incl. RDS for SQL Server), a standalone AD supporting Office 365, or an LDAP directory for Linux applications.
General FAQ: each directory is deployed across multiple AZs, monitoring detects and replaces failed domain controllers, data replication and automated daily snapshots are configured for you.
FAQ under multi-region replication: you cannot remove the primary Region unless you delete the directory.
Multi-Region page Failover and AWS services sections state both parts verbatim.
Important box: can only extend to additional Regions if the primary Region is an AWS default Region; an opt-in primary cannot add Regions.

Multi-Region page: native AD replication; replicates all customer directory data including users, groups, group policies and schema; creates two domain controllers in the selected VPC in the new Region; Enterprise-only scope stated there.
FAQ: feature available in Enterprise Edition only, usable for new and existing directories.
FAQ: directory_id remains the same in the new region and is deployed in the same AWS account as the primary Region.
FAQ: share per Region; directory sharing configurations are not automatically replicated from the primary region.
Multi-Region page: creates two domain controllers in the selected VPC in the new Region in the same account, directory_id same across Regions, more DCs can be added later.
Example 1 (Enterprise, US East Ohio, two DCs): note says hourly cost per managed directory $0.40 per hour and the bill shows two domain controllers at $0.20 per hour each.
Example 2 (Enterprise, Ohio): shared directory hours counted per account (720 x 3 accounts) and billed at $0.06 per shared directory hour.
Pricing page: table lists hourly cost per managed directory, bill lists each domain controller as an individual line item, billed at the per-directory rate plus any additional domain controllers.
Pricing page (Enterprise Edition multi-region): charge per GB for data transferred out of your domain controllers to other Regions where the directory is deployed.
Directory Sharing pricing: hourly charge per additional account; no sharing charge for additional VPCs or the account where the directory is installed.
Pricing page intro states both parts verbatim.
AD Connector quotas: default 10; general quotas page: each supported Region 10, adjustable Yes, per current Region.
